title: Supernova microlensing as a probe of ultracompact minihalos and primordial cosmology
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures
summary: We propose using supernova microlensing to search for ultracompact minihalos and other extended dark structures seeded by enhanced primordial small-scale power. Unlike conventional microlensing searches, which are often optimized for primordial black holes, cosmological supernovae are sensitive to lenses with physical sizes comparable to their Einstein radii (up to $\sim {\rm pc}\left(M/10^4M_\odot\right)^{1/2}$ scale), opening a qualitatively different region of dark object parameter space. We compute the extended object detection efficiency relative to point lenses. We then show how projected limits on the abundance of ultracompact minihalos can be mapped, in benchmark formation scenarios, onto constraints on the primordial power spectrum. With the Vera C. Rubin Observatory expected to deliver an unprecedented LSST supernova sample, supernova microlensing is poised to become a timely and complementary probe of small-scale structure and the physics of the early Universe.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using supernova microlensing to search for ultracompact minihalos and other extended dark structures seeded by enhanced primordial small-scale power, opening a qualitatively new region of dark object parameter space sensitive to lenses with sizes up to ~parsec scales.
AI.motivation: Conventional microlensing searches are optimized for primordial black holes and insensitive to extended dark objects. The authors seek a complementary observational probe for ultracompact minihalos and other extended dark structures seeded by enhanced primordial small-scale power.
AI.method: The authors compute the extended object detection efficiency relative to point lenses for supernova microlensing, accounting for lenses with physical sizes comparable to their Einstein radii. They also map projected abundance limits on ultracompact minihalos onto constraints on the primordial power spectrum using benchmark formation scenarios.
AI.result: The analysis demonstrates that cosmological supernovae are sensitive to extended dark structures with physical sizes up to ~pc(M/10^4 M_sun)^(1/2) scale, and that projected limits on ultracompact minihalo abundance can be converted to constraints on the primordial power spectrum in benchmark formation scenarios.
AI.conclusion: With the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST expected to deliver an unprecedented supernova sample, supernova microlensing is poised to become a timely and complementary probe of small-scale structure and early Universe physics.

title: It's All About the Environment: Local $f_{\rm NL}$ from a Dark Matter Conditioned Multitracer Analysis
comment: 16 + 14 pages, 5 + 3 figures, comments welcome
summary: Primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) offers a powerful test of inflationary physics beyond the simplest single-field scenarios. In large-scale structure, biased tracers respond to local-type PNG with a distinctive scale-dependent signature that is strongest on large scales, but single-tracer measurements are fundamentally limited by cosmic variance. Multitracer methods can mitigate this limitation; however, many existing proposals require splitting tracers using a wide range of halo masses which are often not available, or using secondary halo properties that are not directly observable. Here we develop and validate an alternative strategy based on splitting a tracer sample by its large-scale dark matter environment. We derive a theoretical framework for the $f_{\rm NL}$ response of environmentally selected tracers and test it in $N$-body simulations, confirming consistency between separate-universe predictions and direct power-spectrum inference. To enable observational implementation, we show that a simple linear-theory reconstruction of the dark matter environment from halos yields unbiased $f_{\rm NL}$ constraints in $\mathtt{Quijote}$ simulations. Forecasts for the DESI LRG sample indicate that environmental multitracing can improve constraints on local PNG by a factor of 2-3 relative to conventional single-tracer analyses for high density tracers, comparable to gains achieved when halo formation time is assumed to be perfectly known. We develop an analytic model explaining why the gains are smaller for a halo environment split and why separate-universe predictions fail in this case. Unlike approaches that require modeling assembly bias or inferring secondary halo properties, our method relies only on linear theory. These results establish environmental multitracer techniques as a promising route toward $σ(f_{\rm NL})\sim 1$ with upcoming galaxy surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper develops and validates an environmental multitracer strategy to constrain primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG), where a tracer sample is split by its large-scale dark matter environment. Using linear-theory reconstruction of the environment from halos, the method achieves unbiased f_NL constraints in Quijote simulations and forecasts 2-3x improvements for DESI LRG samples over single-tracer analyses, comparable to gains from perfect knowledge of halo formation time.
AI.motivation: Single-tracer measurements of local-type PNG in large-scale structure are fundamentally limited by cosmic variance. Multitracer methods can mitigate this, but existing proposals require either a wide range of halo masses that are often unavailable, or secondary halo properties (e.g., assembly bias) that are not directly observable. The authors aim to develop an alternative approach that splits tracers by large-scale environment, requiring only linear theory for implementation.
AI.method: The authors derive a theoretical framework for the f_NL response of environmentally selected tracers. They validate it using N-body simulations, comparing separate-universe predictions with direct power-spectrum inference. They demonstrate that a simple linear-theory reconstruction of the dark matter environment from halos yields unbiased f_NL constraints in Quijote simulations, and perform forecasts for the DESI LRG sample. An analytic model is developed to explain cases where gains are smaller (halo environment split) and where separate-universe predictions fail.
AI.result: Environmental multitracing yields unbiased f_NL constraints in Quijote simulations using linear-theory environment reconstruction. Forecasts for DESI LRG samples show a factor of 2-3 improvement over single-tracer analyses for high-density tracers, comparable to gains achieved with perfect knowledge of halo formation time. The analytic model explains reduced gains for halo environment splits and the failure of separate-universe predictions in that regime.
AI.conclusion: Environmental multitracer techniques, relying only on linear theory and not requiring assembly bias modeling or secondary halo properties, represent a promising route toward σ(f_NL) ~ 1 with upcoming galaxy surveys.

title: Model Predictive Scoring Shows Specific BAO Observations (not SNIa) Drives $w_0w_a$ Tension
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables, Submitted to ApJL
summary: The recent analyses of DESI DR2 BAO, Planck CMB and various Supernovae datasets have shown preferences for evolving dark energy at various levels of significance, under frequentist model comparison tests. However, the same analysis done with a pure Bayesian model comparison test can lead to the opposite conclusion due to the impact of $w_0w_a$ priors. In contrast to these in-sample model comparison route, we approach the problem along a third axis -- which model better predicts unseen data. We use the Expected Log Predictive Density (ELPD) metric to score the predictiveness of $Λ$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM models, using the leave-one-redshift-block-out cross-validation estimator. The comparison metric $Δ$ELPD is out-of-sample, unlike $Δχ^2_{\rm MAP}$ and Bayes Factor, and insensitive to prior width, unlike the Bayes factor. Aggregated, we find modest preferences for $w_0 w_a$CDM, primarily driven by the BAO. Decomposing the $Δ$ELPD score by redshift we find that a single BAO block, LRG2 ($z = 0.706$), supplies the entire BAO preference. Interestingly, the biggest outlier point, LRG1, contributes little to the model predictive scoring because both $Λ$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM fail to predict the observation by equal amount. On the other hand, all SNIa datasets' $Δ$ELPD scores are consistent with $0$, indicating that at an out-of-distribution predictive level, the $w_0w_a$CDM tension is entirely driven by one BAO point, not SNIa.

AI.tldr: The paper evaluates whether evolving dark energy ($w_0w_a$CDM) or $\Lambda$CDM better predicts unseen data using the Expected Log Predictive Density (ELPD) metric with leave-one-redshift-block-out cross-validation on DESI DR2 BAO, Planck CMB, and Supernovae datasets. Unlike $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm MAP}$ and Bayes Factor, this out-of-sample metric is insensitive to prior width. The authors find modest preference for $w_0w_a$CDM driven entirely by a single BAO block (LRG2 at $z=0.706$), with SNIa contributions consistent with zero, suggesting the dark energy tension is localized to one data point rather than widespread.
AI.motivation: Recent analyses show conflicting conclusions about evolving dark energy depending on whether frequentist ($\Delta\chi^2_{\rm MAP}$) or Bayesian (Bayes Factor) model comparison is used, with the latter sensitive to $w_0w_a$ prior choices. The authors seek a third, more robust axis: out-of-sample predictive performance, which is both prior-insensitive and avoid in-sample overfitting biases.
AI.method: The authors use the Expected Log Predictive Density (ELPD) metric with a leave-one-redshift-block-out cross-validation estimator to score and compare $\Lambda$CDM versus $w_0w_a$CDM models across DESI DR2 BAO, Planck CMB, and multiple Supernovae datasets. The $\Delta$ELPD score is decomposed by redshift bin to identify which data points drive model preference.
AI.result: Aggregated results show modest preference for $w_0w_a$CDM, driven predominantly by BAO data. Decomposition reveals that a single BAO block, LRG2 ($z=0.706$), accounts for the entire BAO preference. The largest outlier (LRG1) contributes negligibly because both models fail equally. All SNIa datasets show $\Delta$ELPD scores consistent with zero, indicating no predictive advantage for $w_0w_a$CDM from supernovae.
AI.conclusion: At the out-of-sample predictive level, the apparent tension favoring evolving dark energy in the $w_0w_a$ parameterization is driven entirely by one BAO data point (LRG2 at $z=0.706$), not by Supernovae or other BAO measurements. This localization suggests the evolving dark energy signal may be less robust than in-sample analyses suggest, warranting scrutiny of this specific data point or alternative explanations.

title: The Super-Sample Covariance of Line-Intensity Mapping Power Spectrum
comment: 36 Pages (27 main-text- and 4 appendix-pages), 9 Figures
summary: In this work, we provide the first derivation of the line-intensity mapping (LIM) power spectrum super-sample covariance (SSC) from first principles, and also derive as a by-product the non-Gaussian in-box contributions to the covariance for the first time. Previous studies have typically modelled the LIM power spectrum covariance using either the Gaussian approximation or estimates obtained from mocks or the data itself, neglecting uncertainties related to whether the limited volume surveyed sits in a cosmological overdensity. This contribution, known as the SSC or, depending on the context, the field-to-field variance, cannot be estimated from the data, but it is crucial for a correct inference of global quantities, i.e., for ensemble-averaged parameters rather than the actual values just within the patch of the Universe observed. For our derivation, we employ a combination of the halo model and standard perturbation theory that allows us to capture the nonlinearity and non-Gaussianity of the covariance. After a successful validation of our predictions against painted N-body simulations, we explore different scenarios related to current and future LIM experiments, quantifying the relative importance of the non-Gaussian in-box and SSC. We find that the newly derived contributions to the LIM power spectrum covariance are crucial at intermediate and small scales, especially for cases in which the covariance is not dominated by instrumental noise. We find that the relative relevance of the SSC with respect to the other covariance contributions is roughly independent of the survey volume, but does depend on the specific response of the power spectrum to large-scale modes for each line and redshift. Therefore, the impact of the SSC will be increasingly significant for parameter inference from the current and the next generation high signal-to-noise LIM surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper provides the first first-principles derivation of the super-sample covariance (SSC) for the line-intensity mapping (LIM) power spectrum, alongside a derivation of non-Gaussian in-box covariance contributions, using halo model combined with standard perturbation theory. The predictions are validated against N-body simulations, and the authors find that these newly derived covariance contributions are crucial at intermediate and small scales, with SSC impact growing for high signal-to-noise current and future LIM surveys.
AI.motivation: Previous LIM power spectrum covariance studies relied on Gaussian approximations, mocks, or data itself, failing to account for the uncertainty from the surveyed volume sitting in a cosmological overdensity (SSC/field-to-field variance). This contribution cannot be estimated from observational data yet is essential for correctly inferring global (ensemble-averaged) cosmological parameters rather than values specific to the observed patch.
AI.method: The authors combine the halo model with standard perturbation theory to derive the LIM power spectrum SSC and non-Gaussian in-box covariance contributions from first principles. This approach captures the nonlinearity and non-Gaussianity of the covariance. Validation is performed against painted N-body simulations, and various current/future LIM experimental scenarios are explored.
AI.result: The newly derived covariance contributions are found to be crucial at intermediate and small scales, especially when covariance is not dominated by instrumental noise. The relative importance of SSC versus other covariance contributions is roughly independent of survey volume but depends on the specific response of the power spectrum to large-scale modes for each emission line and redshift.
AI.conclusion: The SSC will be increasingly significant for parameter inference from current and next-generation high signal-to-noise LIM surveys, warranting proper incorporation of these covariance terms in future analyses.

title: JWST/NIRSpec Reveals Diverse Nuclear Environments in Dwarf Galaxies Hosting AGN
comment: 27 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables. Accepted to ApJ
summary: Dwarf galaxies, in the $Λ$CDM framework, are expected to dominate the galaxy number density at all redshifts. As such, studying AGN in these systems, including characterizing their local environments and emission properties, is essential in obtaining a comprehensive view of the AGN population and their influence on their host galaxy. To this end, we present JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of four dwarf galaxies (M$_\star<$10$^{9.5}\;$M$_\odot$) with evidence of AGN activity. Utilizing the improvements in resolution and sensitivity offered by JWST, we investigate the emission features of the central kiloparsec of these dwarfs. Our findings include the detection of over 100 emission lines across our sample, including coronal lines with ionization potentials greater than 300 eV. The nuclear spectra show diverse emission features. In two galaxies, we measure strong contributions from hot dust to the infrared continuum. We also detect both PAH and coronal line emission within 100 parsecs of the nuclei in three galaxies. We estimate the hot H$_2$ gas mass to be between 1--20 M$_\odot$ within 300 pc across our sample, where both thermal and non-thermal excitation are involved. Lastly, spatial flux maps reveal varied emission structures across all observed gas phases, ranging from radial symmetry around the nucleus to elongated plumes. Kinematic maps also show each galaxy has unique velocity structures despite all being isolated, affirming the diversity of rotation curves problem, a long standing tension between simulations and observations. These results showcase the unique and varied nuclear environments that can be found in dwarf galaxies hosting AGN.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of four dwarf galaxies (M_*<10^9.5 M_sun) with AGN activity reveal over 100 emission lines, including coronal lines with ionization potentials >300 eV, hot dust contributions to IR continuum, PAH and coronal line emission within 100 pc of nuclei in three galaxies, hot H2 gas masses of 1-20 M_sun within 300 pc, and diverse spatial/kinematic morphologies that illustrate the variety of nuclear environments in AGN-hosting dwarf galaxies.
AI.motivation: Dwarf galaxies are expected to dominate the galaxy number density in the ΛCDM framework, yet AGN in these systems remain poorly characterized. Understanding their local environments and emission properties is essential for a comprehensive view of the AGN population and their feedback effects on host galaxies, especially given tensions like the diversity of rotation curves problem between simulations and observations.
AI.method: JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations targeting the central kiloparsec of four dwarf galaxies (M_*<10^9.5 M_sun) with evidence of AGN activity, leveraging JWST's improved resolution and sensitivity to analyze emission features, including spectral line identification, infrared continuum characterization, hot H2 gas mass estimation, and spatial/kinematic mapping across multiple gas phases.
AI.result: Detection of over 100 emission lines across the sample, including coronal lines with ionization potentials >300 eV. Two galaxies show strong hot dust contributions to the infrared continuum. PAH and coronal line emission are detected within 100 pc of nuclei in three galaxies. Hot H2 gas masses range between 1-20 M_sun within 300 pc, excited by both thermal and non-thermal mechanisms. Spatial flux maps reveal varied emission structures from radial symmetry to elongated plumes, and kinematic maps show unique velocity structures per galaxy despite all being isolated.
AI.conclusion: These findings showcase the unique and varied nuclear environments found in dwarf galaxies hosting AGN, highlighting the diversity of their emission properties and kinematic structures, and confirming the diversity of rotation curves problem as a persistent tension between simulations and observations.

title: Implementation of frequency-correlated noise in CMB component separation: Method, Validation, and Early Applications
summary: Parametric component separation methods used in cosmic microwave background (CMB) analyses commonly assume instrumental noise to be uncorrelated between frequency channels. This approximation may become insufficient for experiments whose design naturally introduces cross-channel correlations, such as interferometric or multi-band bolometric systems. This work aims to provide a consistent framework to include frequency-correlated noise in Commander2 and to quantify its impact on component separation in controlled and instrument-motivated simulations. We generalized the amplitude sampling of the Commander2 framework to consistently handle dense frequency-frequency noise covariance matrices, modifying the likelihood evaluation and parallel architecture. The implementation is validated on low-resolution simulations of a simplified CMB-S4-like configuration. We applied the generalized framework to instrument-motivated simulations of the QUBIC bolometric interferometer, using representative noise models derived from end-to-end simulations. Validation tests show excellent convergence and agreement between sampled parameters and analytical maximum-likelihood estimates. Accounting for frequency correlations reduces the width of the maximum-likelihood residual distributions by up to 8% on average, and up to 11% for individual parameters, relative to the diagonal-noise approximation. In QUBIC-based simulations, accounting for an anti-correlated noise produces posterior widths reduced by about 60%, while a positive-correlation test increases them by about 40%. This shows that neglecting cross-channel correlations can lead to incorrect posterior estimates in either direction. The generalized implementation presented here enables the Commander2 software to consistently propagate such correlations into parameter estimation, providing a framework for assessing their impact in future CMB analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes the Commander2 CMB component separation framework to handle dense frequency-frequency noise covariance matrices, enabling proper treatment of cross-channel noise correlations that are characteristic of instruments like interferometers and multi-band bolometers. The implementation is validated on CMB-S4-like and QUBIC simulations, showing that neglecting these correlations can bias posterior widths in either direction (up to ~60% reduction or ~40% increase depending on the correlation sign).
AI.motivation: Parametric component separation methods in CMB analyses typically assume instrumental noise is uncorrelated between frequency channels. This approximation breaks down for instruments with natural cross-channel correlations, such as interferometric or multi-band bolometric systems, potentially leading to incorrect posterior estimates.
AI.method: The authors generalized the amplitude sampling module of the Commander2 framework to consistently handle dense frequency-frequency noise covariance matrices, including modifications to the likelihood evaluation and parallel architecture. The framework was validated on low-resolution simulations of a simplified CMB-S4-like configuration and applied to instrument-motivated QUBIC bolometric interferometer simulations with representative noise models from end-to-end simulations.

AI.conclusion: Neglecting cross-channel noise correlations can lead to incorrect posterior estimates in either direction. The generalized Commander2 implementation consistently propagates such correlations into parameter estimation, providing a framework for assessing their impact in future CMB analyses.

title: Super-Eddington Accretion and Early-Stage Feedback in Ton S180
comment: 15 pages (main text), 8 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A (1 September 2026)
summary: Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies are key laboratories for studying rapid supermassive black hole (SMBH) growth and active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback at high accretion rates. We investigate the nearby NLSy1 Ton S180 with VLT-MUSE optical integral field spectroscopy to connect its nuclear accretion properties with the spatially resolved ionized gas and host-galaxy kinematics. We modeled the unresolved nuclear spectrum and applied a custom point spread function subtraction to recover the host-galaxy emission on kiloparsec scales. The nuclear spectrum requires a complex permitted-line decomposition and a blueshifted [O III] outflow component. Single-epoch estimators and the stellar velocity dispersion imply black hole masses in the range $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot) = 6.5 - 7.7$. Combined with the observed luminosity, this implies a dimensionless mass accretion rate of $\dot{M} / \dot{M}_{\rm Edd} = 4.1 - 980$, confirming the extreme accretion regime. The host galaxy shows a circumnuclear ring, an inner elongated structure consistent with a bar, and rotation-dominated gas and stellar kinematics. Simple inflow models do not significantly better reproduce the observed velocity field. We detect a resolved ionized outflow extending about 2 kpc west of the nucleus, with mildly blueshifted velocities (with a maximum of $v_{\rm max} \sim 340$ km s$^{-1}$). Its mass outflow rate is only $\sim 4.2 \times 10^{-4}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, whereas the unresolved nuclear outflow reaches $v_{\rm max} \sim 1140$ km s$^{-1}$ and $\dot{M}_{\rm out} > 1.5\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. This contrast may reflect either weak ionized coupling from nuclear to galactic scales or different episodes of AGN activity over time. These results show that Ton S180 is undergoing rapid SMBH growth, while the observed ionized outflow remains confined to the inner few kiloparsecs and is weak on host-galaxy scales.

AI.tldr: This study uses VLT-MUSE optical integral field spectroscopy to investigate the nearby NLSy1 galaxy Ton S180, connecting its nuclear accretion properties with spatially resolved ionized gas and host-galaxy kinematics. The galaxy exhibits extreme super-Eddington accretion (mass accretion rate 4.1–980 times Eddington) with black hole masses in the range log(M_BH/M_sun) = 6.5–7.7. While a resolved ionized outflow extends ~2 kpc west of the nucleus with modest velocities, the nuclear outflow is much faster and more massive. The host galaxy shows rotation-dominated kinematics with a circumnuclear ring and bar-like structure, and the ionized outflow remains confined to the inner few kiloparsecs, indicating rapid SMBH growth but weak coupling of outflows to host-galaxy scales.
AI.motivation: NLSy1 galaxies are key laboratories for studying rapid supermassive black hole growth and AGN feedback at high accretion rates. The study aims to connect nuclear accretion properties with spatially resolved ionized gas and host-galaxy kinematics in Ton S180 to understand how extreme accretion manifests across galactic scales.

They modeled the unresolved nuclear spectrum, applied custom point spread function subtraction to recover host-galaxy emission on kiloparsec scales, performed complex permitted-line decomposition with a blueshifted [O III] outflow component, used single-epoch estimators and stellar velocity dispersion for black hole mass estimates, and analyzed gas and stellar kinematics including outflow properties.

title: Studies on the dark sector interaction from joint analysis of cosmological probes
comment: 20 pages, 6 figures
summary: We test whether constraints on the nonlinear interaction $ξ$IDE are stable under different treatments of the Type Ia supernovae absolute calibration. \textit{Fermi} GRBs measurements and the Amati-relation parameters are fitted jointly with PantheonPlus SNe Ia, DESI DR2 BAO, and an updated cosmic-chronometer compilation. We compare the PantheonPlus-SH0ES route, which retains the SN absolute calibration, with the PantheonPlus-only route, in which the SN absolute magnitude is analytically marginalized. The GOLD GRB sample is adopted for the main analysis, while the FULL GRB sample is used to assess sample dependence. For the interaction parameter $γ\equivξ+3w$, where $γ=0$ denotes the non-interacting limit, the GOLD sample gives $γ=1.453^{+1.297}_{-1.597}$ for the PantheonPlus-SH0ES and $γ=-0.634^{+1.668}_{-2.486}$ for the PantheonPlus-only. Although the posterior medians correspond to opposite directions of energy transfer, neither route excludes $γ=0$ at 68\% credibility, and the reconstructed interaction rate remains consistent with zero over the redshift range considered. Replacing the GOLD sample with the FULL sample produces negligible changes in the interaction constraints. Moreover, $w$CDM and CPL achieve likelihood improvements comparable to that of $ξ$IDE, while the information criteria do not consistently favor the interacting model. A redshift-bin diagnostic finds no significant redshift evolution of the Amati relation. We find no compelling evidence for a dark sector interaction that is robust to the choice of SN calibration or specifically favored over noninteracting dark energy extensions.

AI.tldr: This paper tests the stability of constraints on the nonlinear dark sector interaction parameter ξIDE under different Type Ia supernova absolute calibration treatments. Using Fermi GRBs, PantheonPlus SNe Ia, DESI DR2 BAO, and cosmic chronometers, the authors compare two calibration routes (PantheonPlus-SH0ES retaining SN calibration vs. PantheonPlus-only with marginalization). Neither route excludes the non-interacting limit γ=0 at 68% credibility, the interaction rate is consistent with zero, results are insensitive to GRB sample choice, and non-interacting models (wCDM, CPL) achieve comparable likelihood improvements as ξIDE without consistent preference. No compelling evidence for a dark sector interaction robust to SN calibration exists.
AI.motivation: To determine whether previously reported evidence for dark sector interactions (ξIDE) is robust or instead depends on the treatment of Type Ia supernova absolute magnitude calibration, which is a known source of systematic uncertainty in cosmological analyses.
AI.method: Jointly fit Fermi GRB measurements and Amati-relation parameters with PantheonPlus SNe Ia, DESI DR2 BAO, and an updated cosmic-chronometer compilation. Compare two SN calibration schemes: PantheonPlus-SH0ES (retains absolute calibration) and PantheonPlus-only (absolute magnitude analytically marginalized). Use GOLD GRB sample for main analysis and FULL sample for robustness. Employ redshift-bin diagnostics for Amati relation evolution and information criteria for model comparison against wCDM and CPL.
AI.result: The interaction parameter γ gives γ=1.453(+1.297/-1.597) for PantheonPlus-SH0ES and γ=-0.634(+1.668/-2.486) for PantheonPlus-only, with posterior medians in opposite directions but neither excluding γ=0 at 68% credibility. The reconstructed interaction rate is consistent with zero across the redshift range. Replacing GOLD with FULL GRB sample yields negligible changes, no significant Amati-relation redshift evolution is found, and information criteria do not consistently favor the interacting ξIDE model over wCDM/CPL.
AI.conclusion: There is no compelling evidence for a dark sector interaction that is robust to SN absolute calibration choice or specifically favored over non-interacting dark energy extensions (wCDM, CPL). The interaction constraints are not stable across calibration treatments, undermining claims of a detected dark sector interaction.

title: Resolved Dust-Gas-Metallicity relations in nearby spiral galaxies
comment: 23 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Resubmitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Context: Understanding the interstellar medium (ISM) requires high-resolution, multi-component mapping to capture its complex physical structure. Nearby spiral galaxies, with their abundant and diverse ISM, provide an ideal laboratory for such a comprehensive analysis at sub-galactic scales. Aims: We investigate dust-to-gas (DGR) and dust-to-metal (DMR) ratios as a functions of gas-phase metallicity (Z), on spatial scales ranging from 0.6 to 2.3 kpc, in a sample of 10 nearby spiral galaxies, spanning more than an order of magnitude in stellar mass (9.7 \le \log(M_*/M_\odot) \leq 11.0), star formation rate (SFR, \sim 0.3--3 \, M_\odot \, \rm yr^{-1}) and metallicity ranging from 8.3 \lesssim 12 + \log( O/H) \lesssim 8.8. We explore how the DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations are shaped by the assumptions behind the CO-to-H_2 conversion factor (α_{CO}). Methods: We homogeneously combine maps of dust, atomic gas, molecular gas, and metallicity. Motivated by the diversity in L_{CO(1-0)}/SFR ratios and metallicity across our sample, we introduce a hybrid α_{CO} prescription to distinguish between CO-bright and CO-dark regimes. The derived DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations are compared with other global and resolved observational results, and with the predictions of dust and chemical evolution models. Results: Both DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations are dependent on the adopted α_{CO} prescription, and no single α_{CO} can reproduce the properties of the entire sample, motivating the use of a hybrid approach. The DGR increases with metallicity, spanning \sim 1 dex across the sampled range; while the DMR remains approximately constant at \log(\mathrm{DMR}) = -0.53 \pm 0.13, implying that \sim 30 \% of metals are locked into dust grains. This flat behavior indicates an evolved dust phase where efficient ISM grain growth drives a saturation regime balancing dust formation and destruction.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes dust-to-gas (DGR) and dust-to-metal (DMR) ratios as functions of metallicity across 0.6-2.3 kpc scales in 10 nearby spiral galaxies. Using a new hybrid CO-to-H2 conversion factor prescription, they find DGR increases ~1 dex with metallicity while DMR remains flat at log(DMR) = -0.53 ± 0.13 (~30% of metals locked in dust), indicating an evolved dust phase with efficient grain growth in saturation.
AI.motivation: Understanding the complex physical structure of the interstellar medium requires high-resolution, multi-component mapping. Nearby spiral galaxies serve as ideal laboratories for investigating dust-to-gas and dust-to-metal relationships at sub-galactic scales, particularly how these relations depend on gas-phase metallicity and CO-to-H2 conversion assumptions.
AI.method: The authors homogeneously combine maps of dust, atomic gas, molecular gas, and metallicity across 10 nearby spiral galaxies spanning a wide range of stellar mass, SFR, and metallicity. They introduce a hybrid α_CO prescription distinguishing CO-bright from CO-dark regimes, motivated by diversity in L_CO/SFR ratios and metallicity, then compare derived DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations with other observations and model predictions.
AI.result: Both DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations depend strongly on the adopted α_CO prescription, with no single prescription fitting the full sample. DGR increases with metallicity spanning ~1 dex across the sampled range. DMR remains approximately constant at log(DMR) = -0.53 ± 0.13, implying ~30% of metals are locked into dust grains.
AI.conclusion: The flat DMR-metallicity relation indicates an evolved dust phase where efficient ISM grain growth drives a saturation regime balancing dust formation and destruction. The hybrid α_CO approach is necessary to properly capture dust scaling relations across diverse galaxy populations.

title: A guide to choosing data compression methods for cosmological inference
comment: 18 pages, 14 figures. Submitted to RASTI
summary:
We provide a pedagogical guide to help researchers choose an appropriate compression method for cosmological inference and numerical covariance estimation, trading off the balance between information loss and complexity. We describe methods used in the literature, categorising them by the form of the loss function -- Fisher information, mutual information, or mean squared error -- and by whether they are linear or non-linear.
  We consider in detail the linear compression methods: massively optimised parameter estimation and data compression (MOPED), canonical correlation analysis (CCA), principal component analysis, and linear neural networks. We also investigate simple non-linear methods based on neural networks with similar architectures but different loss functions. We use tomographic weak lensing power spectra as example data vectors, deriving constraints on the cosmological parameters $Ω_\mathrm{m}$, $σ_8$, $w_0$ and $w_a$ from compressed data. For our figure of merit (FoM) we use the log determinant of the Fisher matrix, which approximates the covariance of the full posterior well. MOPED and a Fisher information-based linear neural network both achieve lossless compression. Neural networks with loss functions which optimise mutual information achieve at most 84 per cent of the uncompressed FoM and those which minimise mean squared errors achieve at most 72 per cent. We show how to determine whether MOPED will retain information even if the fiducial cosmology is not known with certainty, and demonstrate a strategy for CCA which results in an FoM close to that of MOPED while requiring only an approximate idea of where the bulk of the posterior mass is located.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a pedagogical guide to choosing data compression methods for cosmological inference and covariance estimation, comparing linear methods (MOPED, CCA, PCA, linear neural networks) and non-linear neural network approaches with different loss functions (Fisher information, mutual information, MSE). Using tomographic weak lensing power spectra, they find MOPED and Fisher-based linear neural networks achieve lossless compression, while mutual information-based methods reach at most 84% and MSE-based at most 72% of the uncompressed figure of merit. They also provide strategies for when the fiducial cosmology is uncertain.
AI.motivation: To help researchers choose an appropriate compression method for cosmological inference and numerical covariance estimation by systematically comparing methods and understanding the trade-off between information loss and complexity.
AI.method: Methods are categorized by loss function (Fisher information, mutual information, or mean squared error) and by linearity (linear vs. non-linear). Linear methods including MOPED, CCA, PCA, and linear neural networks are analyzed in detail, alongside non-linear neural networks sharing architectures but differing in loss functions. Tomographic weak lensing power spectra serve as test data, with constraints on Ωm, σ8, w0, and wa derived from compressed data using the log determinant of the Fisher matrix as the figure of merit.
AI.result: MOPED and Fisher information-based linear neural networks achieve lossless compression. Mutual information-based neural networks achieve at most 84% of the uncompressed FoM, while MSE-minimizing networks achieve at most 72%. The work also demonstrates how to assess whether MOPED retains information when the fiducial cosmology is uncertain and presents a CCA strategy achieving FoM close to MOPED with only approximate knowledge of the posterior location.
AI.conclusion: Loss functions based on Fisher information (e.g., MOPED and Fisher-based linear neural networks) provide lossless compression for this application, outperforming mutual information- and MSE-based approaches. Practical guidance is provided for choosing compression methods, including robustness strategies when the fiducial cosmology is not precisely known and when only approximate posterior location information is available (CCA).

title: AGN-DB: A Unified Multi-Wavelength Database of Active Galactic Nuclei
comment: Submitted to ApJ. Comments and inputs from the community are very welcome!
summary: We present the Active Galactic Nuclei Database (AGN-DB), a comprehensive, multi-wavelength catalog compiled from more than 100 publicly available AGN catalogs and samples released by the end of 2025, spanning radio to $γ$-ray wavelengths. The database contains approximately 8.1 million unique sources, approximately 7.8 million of which remain after flagging stellar contaminants, and approximately 6.8 million of these are classified as AGN. Source cross-matching across catalogs is performed using Lyra, a Bayesian likelihood-ratio framework that jointly considers positional uncertainties, source densities, and photometric information to compute posterior match probabilities. The resulting catalog provides astrometric coordinates, redshifts, photometry, and classifications for each unique source. All multi-catalog provenance is preserved. For every property, we store the full array of values and originating catalog identifiers, enabling multi-epoch and multi-survey analyses. In this paper, we describe the AGN-DB pipeline, including the cross-matching methodology, and present the statistical properties of the v1.0 catalog. AGN-DB is designed to enable population studies, spectral energy distribution modeling, AGN classification, and variability analyses at an unprecedented scale. Its pipeline is designed to facilitate the integration of new catalogs, allowing AGN-DB to be updated regularly, with releases planned at least annually.

AI.tldr: AGN-DB is a comprehensive multi-wavelength catalog of ~8.1 million unique sources (6.8 million classified as AGN), assembled from more than 100 public AGN catalogs using Lyra, a Bayesian likelihood-ratio cross-matching framework. It provides astrometric coordinates, redshifts, photometry, and classifications with full provenance tracking, designed for large-scale population studies, SED modeling, classification, and variability analyses.
AI.motivation: To create a unified, comprehensive AGN catalog that integrates disparate multi-wavelength datasets into a single resource, enabling large-scale population studies and analyses that would otherwise require cumbersome cross-referencing of many individual catalogs.
AI.method: Cross-matching of over 100 public AGN catalogs using Lyra, a Bayesian likelihood-ratio framework incorporating positional uncertainties, source densities, and photometric information to compute posterior match probabilities. The pipeline preserves provenance and stores full arrays of values with originating catalog identifiers for every property.
AI.result: The v1.0 catalog contains approximately 8.1 million unique sources, ~7.8 million after flagging stellar contaminants, and ~6.8 million classified as AGN, spanning radio to gamma-ray wavelengths.
AI.conclusion: AGN-DB enables unprecedented-scale population studies, spectral energy distribution modeling, AGN classification, and variability analyses. Its modular pipeline supports regular (at least annual) updates with new catalog integrations.

title: Late-Time Emergence of Dark Energy and Its Interaction with Dark Matter
comment: 15 pages including references; 10 captioned figures and 3 tables; version accepted by Phys. Rev. D
summary: We present an interacting scenario between dark energy (DE) and dark matter (DM), where DE has an emergent nature, that means, DE was absent in the early universe but it becomes effective only at late times. We consider two specific emergent DE models, one with no free parameters and the other featuring two parameters describing the speed and epoch of the transition. We constrain both scenarios using the cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements from the Planck 2018 release, baryon acoustic oscillations from DESI DR2, and three different compilations of Type Ia supernovae (PantheonPlus, DES-Dovekie, and Union3). Our analysis indicates that current cosmological probes are not able to tightly constrain the speed of the transition. For both scenarios, the posterior distribution of the interaction parameter is shifted away from zero at more than 95\% CL whenever the CMB data are combined with any of these additional probes, with the preferred direction corresponding to a transfer of energy from DE to DM. While CMB alone yields a high value of $H_0$, in agreement with local determinations, this effect is reduced when DESI is added and disappears once supernova data are included. In contrast, the clustering parameter $S_8$ is consistently shifted toward lower values in the combined datasets, and it is correlated with the preference for a negative interaction. However, according to the $Δχ^2_{\rm min}$ and Bayesian evidence, none of the interacting models is favored over $Λ$CDM or $w_0w_a$CDM, indicating that the interaction does not rescue these emergent DE models. Our results therefore highlight the limitations of these scenarios in addressing current cosmological tensions, while pointing to the crucial role of future data in further assessing their viability.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes interacting emergent dark energy (DE) models, where DE is absent in the early universe and emerges only at late times, using Planck 2018 CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and three Type Ia supernova compilations (PantheonPlus, DES-Dovekie, Union3). Results show the interaction parameter is preferred away from zero (DE→DM transfer) at >95% CL when CMB is combined with any additional probe, and S8 is consistently shifted lower. However, none of the interacting emergent DE models is statistically favored over ΛCDM or w0waCDM, and the models fail to resolve current cosmological tensions.
AI.motivation: To test whether emergent dark energy models, extended with an interaction between dark energy and dark matter, can address current cosmological tensions (the H0 and S8 discrepancies) given that standard interacting DE models and emergent scenarios face challenges with observations.
AI.method: Two emergent DE models are considered: one with no free parameters and one with two parameters controlling transition speed and epoch. The scenarios are constrained via Markov Chain Monte Carlo analyses using Planck 2018 CMB data, DESI DR2 BAO, and three independent Type Ia supernova compilations (PantheonPlus, DES-Dovekie, Union3). Model comparison is performed using Δχ²_min and Bayesian evidence against ΛCDM and w0waCDM baselines.
AI.result: Current cosmological probes cannot tightly constrain the transition speed in either model. The interaction parameter's posterior shifts away from zero at >95% CL whenever CMB is combined with any additional probe, favoring energy transfer from DE to DM. CMB alone gives high H0 consistent with local measurements, but this is reduced with DESI and disappears with supernova data. S8 is consistently shifted to lower values in combined datasets and correlates with the negative interaction preference. However, neither interacting emergent DE model is favored over ΛCDM or w0waCDM by Δχ²_min or Bayesian evidence.
AI.conclusion: Interacting emergent DE models do not rescue current cosmological tensions; their interaction cannot significantly improve fit over standard cosmological models. The results underscore limitations of these scenarios and highlight the need for future data to further assess their viability.

title: Recovering Ionizing Photon Escape and Galaxy Scaling Relations in the LzLCS via Si II and C II Absorption Lines and Mock Spectra from a Radiation-Hydrodynamic Simulation
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures
summary: In this work, we use a radiation-hydrodynamic simulation of a single $\sim10^9M_{\odot}$ virtual galaxy to study Si II and C II line profiles seen in stacked HST/COS spectra of 58 galaxies from the LzLCS+ sample. We compare stacks across three mass bins ($M_{\star} \leq 10^8M_{\odot}$, $10^8$-$10^9M_{\odot}$, and $M_{\star} \geq 10^9M_{\odot}$) and three stacking methods (mean, median, and weighted average) to a library of 22,500 mock spectra. We investigate whether the simulation can accurately mimic real gas features, reveal clear trends with galaxy properties, and provide indirect estimates of the ionizing escape fraction ($f_{\rm esc}$). We find reasonable agreement between simulated and observed profiles ($χ^2 < 1$) across all mass regimes. Notably, extracting line properties such as EW and $R_f$ from best-fit mock profiles provides a robust alternative to direct empirical trends, particularly in the low-S/N regime where noise frequently biases results. The simulation-based LIS features, although derived from a single virtual object, exhibit clear correlations with $M_{\star}$, SFR, and $f_{\rm esc}$, mirroring established empirical scaling relations. We find that the best-matching mock spectra predominantly originate from simulation time steps corresponding to peak UV luminosity and intense starburst phases, suggesting that these active periods generate the ISM diversity observed in star-forming galaxies. Finally, simulation-based estimates ($f_{\rm esc}^{\rm virtual}$) reproduce the observed mass-dependent trends in $f_{\rm esc}$ and are in close agreement with the average $f_{\rm esc}$ of the generated stacks. This simulation-based framework establishes a relevant methodology for interpreting spectroscopic observations, including inferring $f_{\rm esc}$ and characterizing physical scaling relations, in high-redshift galaxies from the Epoch of Reionization.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a radiation-hydrodynamic simulation of a ~10^9 M_sun virtual galaxy to model Si II and C II line profiles observed in HST/COS spectra of 58 galaxies from the LzLCS+ sample, comparing across mass bins and stacking methods against 22,500 mock spectra. The simulation reproduces observed profiles (chi^2<1), shows that mock spectra provide robust line property estimates in low-S/N regimes, and yields virtual escape fraction estimates (f_esc^virtual) that match observed mass-dependent trends, establishing a framework for interpreting high-redshift Epoch of Reionization galaxies.
AI.motivation: To test whether radiation-hydrodynamic simulations can accurately reproduce low-ionization state (LIS) absorption line profiles in nearby galaxies, and to develop a robust methodology for characterizing physical scaling relations and inferring the ionizing escape fraction, which is critical for understanding the Epoch of Reionization.
AI.method: A single radiation-hydrodynamic simulation (~10^9 M_sun virtual galaxy) is compared to stacked HST/COS spectra of 58 LzLCS+ galaxies. The analysis spans three mass bins and three stacking methods (mean, median, weighted average), with a library of 22,500 mock Si II and C II line profiles generated from simulation time steps. Line properties (EW, R_f) are extracted from best-fit mock profiles and compared to direct empirical measurements, while f_esc^virtual estimates are derived from the best-matching simulation snapshots.
AI.result: Simulated and observed profiles show reasonable agreement (chi^2<1) across all mass regimes. Best-fit mock profiles provide robust line property extraction in low-S/N regimes where noise biases direct measurements. Simulated LIS features exhibit clear correlations with stellar mass, SFR, and f_esc, mirroring empirical scaling relations. Best-matching mock spectra come predominantly from simulation time steps at peak UV luminosity and intense starburst phases. The virtual f_esc estimates reproduce observed mass-dependent trends and agree with the average f_esc of the stacks.
AI.conclusion: This simulation-based framework provides a validated methodology for interpreting LIS spectral observations and inferring f_esc, and can be extended to high-redshift galaxies from the Epoch of Reionization where direct empirical calibrations are not feasible.

title: Expanding the scope of dark siren cosmology: Inferring the population properties of gravitational wave-hosting galaxies
summary: The field of gravitational wave "dark siren" cosmology is facing a number of challenges surrounding the way in which galaxy catalogue data is incorporated into the analysis. The three biggest challenges are adequately compensating for galaxy catalogue incompleteness, robust treatment of galaxy redshift and source properties, and the as-yet unknown host galaxy weighting model. We present an updated methodology for inferring cosmological parameters using dark sirens and incomplete galaxy catalogues. By switching to a sampled redshift prior, rather than one which is pre-computed on a grid, we can jointly infer parameters which describe the population of gravitational-wave hosting galaxies, alongside the gravitational wave population and cosmological model. Using the cosmological inference software gwcosmo, we reproduce a subset of GWTC-5.0 cosmology results, then extend the analysis to jointly infer the host galaxy weighting model - the first measurement of its kind to do so - leading to an updated measurement of the Hubble constant with $H_0 = {71.9}_{-7.5}^{+9.1}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ (median and 68% symmetric credible interval). This innovative new method opens the door to solving several of the biggest challenges currently facing the field of dark siren cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an updated methodology for dark siren cosmology that uses a sampled redshift prior instead of a grid-based one, allowing joint inference of host galaxy weighting parameters, gravitational wave populations, and cosmological parameters. Reproducing GWTC-5.0 results and extending to infer the host galaxy weighting model for the first time, they report an updated Hubble constant measurement of H0 = 71.9 (+9.1/-7.5) km/s/Mpc.
AI.motivation: Dark siren cosmology faces three major challenges: adequately compensating for galaxy catalogue incompleteness, robust treatment of galaxy redshift and source properties, and the unknown host galaxy weighting model. These issues hinder accurate cosmological parameter inference with dark sirens.
AI.method: The authors develop an updated methodology for cosmological inference that replaces the grid-based pre-computed redshift prior with a sampled redshift prior. This enables joint inference of host galaxy population parameters, gravitational wave source population, and cosmological parameters simultaneously. The method is implemented using the gwcosmo software and validated by reproducing GWTC-5.0 cosmology results.
AI.result: The analysis reproduces a subset of GWTC-5.0 cosmology results, then extends to jointly infer the host galaxy weighting model—the first measurement of its kind. This yields an updated Hubble constant measurement of H0 = 71.9 (+9.1/−7.5) km/s/Mpc (median and 68% symmetric credible interval).
AI.conclusion: This new sampled-prior methodology addresses key challenges in dark siren cosmology, particularly the unknown host galaxy weighting model, and opens the door to solving several of the biggest obstacles currently limiting the field's accuracy and robustness.

title: Widespread Inflows Reveal Baryonic Cycling in Star-forming and Quiescent Galaxies
comment: 73 pages, 25 Figures (5 Main + 8 Extended Data + 12 Supplementary), submitted on 6th March 2026
summary: Cool-gas inflows, required to sustain star formation, have been fundamental in simulations yet remained observationally elusive. Using DESI spectroscopy of ~30,000 galaxies, we identify coherent inflowing gas (~100 km/s) in 20-50% of the sample, yielding a population-level census of gas flows. We uncover a striking inversion: inflows are detected in quiescent galaxies, whereas star-forming systems are dominated by gravitationally bound outflows. At fixed age, galaxies with inflows, outflows, or no/weak flows share similar masses, environments, and structures, indicating that these properties do not differentiate flow states. Instead, gas-flow state is linked to stellar population age and recent evolutionary history, consistent with age-dependent gas flows in two regimes. In some star-forming galaxies, elevated star formation surface densities drive outflows that recycle on ~0.5 Gyr timescales, consistent with a galactic fountain. In quiescent systems, low-level ``drizzling'' inflows persist, consistent with slowly cooling enriched halo gas and weak radio-mode nuclear activity. Broad gas-phase metallicity distributions---and absence of a pristine dilution signature---indicate that detected inflows are predominantly recycled or enriched. Detectability is modulated by dust, ionization, and geometry: in star-forming disks, inflowing gas lies near the disk plane and is obscured or ionized, while outflow hosts exhibit higher dust and metal content. As star formation declines, cold-outflow signatures weaken, and recycled or slowly cooling gas is more readily detected as inflow. Post-starburst galaxies provide snapshots of this transition. Our results resolve the scarcity of observed inflows, provide evidence for widespread gas accretion and recycling in present day galaxies, and establish an observational framework linking gas flows to star formation, chemical evolution, and galaxy structure.

AI.tldr: Using DESI spectroscopy of ~30,000 galaxies, the authors identify coherent inflowing gas (~100 km/s) in 20-50% of the sample, revealing an inversion where inflows occur in quiescent galaxies while star-forming systems show gravitationally bound outflows. Gas-flow state is linked to stellar population age and recent evolutionary history, with star-forming galaxies exhibiting galactic fountain outflows that recycle on ~0.5 Gyr timescales, and quiescent systems showing low-level "drizzling" inflows consistent with slowly cooling halo gas. Detectability is modulated by dust, ionization, and geometry.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing observational scarcity of cool-gas inflows that simulations require for sustaining star formation, by providing a population-level census of gas flows in present-day galaxies.
AI.method: Analysis of DESI spectroscopy of ~30,000 galaxies to identify coherent inflowing and outflowing gas signatures at ~100 km/s, combined with comparisons of galaxy properties (mass, environment, structure) and stellar population diagnostics across flow states.
AI.result: Inflows detected in 20-50% of the sample. Striking inversion found: inflows dominate in quiescent galaxies while star-forming galaxies show bound outflows. Flow state correlates with stellar age and recent evolution, not with mass/environment/structure. Two regimes identified: galactic fountains in star-forming galaxies (recycling on ~0.5 Gyr) and drizzling inflows in quiescent systems (cooling halo gas with weak radio-mode AGN). Inflows are predominantly recycled/enriched, with detectability modulated by dust, ionization, and geometry.
AI.conclusion: The results resolve the observational scarcity of inflows, provide widespread evidence for gas accretion and recycling in present-day galaxies, and establish an observational framework linking gas flows to star formation, chemical evolution, and galaxy structure, with post-starburst galaxies serving as transition snapshots.

title: Supernovae Unite: Combining Pantheon+ and DES-SN5YR
comment: 28 pages, 22 figures. The Unite Hubble diagram and likelihood will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the paper
summary: We present the Hubble diagram and cosmological constraints resulting from the combination of the Pantheon+ and DES-SN5YR supernova (SN) samples, which we refer to as Unite. Unite updates Pantheon+, including methodology improvements that the DES sample enabled, and adds the new SN from the DES survey. This represents the most comprehensive and internally consistent SN Ia dataset available, consisting of 2884 likely type Ia supernovae. This work features consistent SN Ia modelling, sample selection, and bias corrections. We also redetermine host-galaxy stellar masses for over 98% of the sample using a consistent framework. Using Unite alone, for a flat universe with a cosmological constant (Flat-$Λ$CDM), we find $Ω_{\rm m} = 0.310^{+0.012}_{-0.011}$. We further present constraints using the Unite sample combined with Cosmic Microwave Background and both DES and DESI Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data. We find strong evidence of tension between CMB measurements and the combined BAO and supernova datasets when fitting a model with constant dark energy equation of state ($w$), which is alleviated when allowing $w$ to vary with time. For a flat universe with dark energy that has a time-evolving equation of state parametrized by $w_0$ and $w_a$ we find $(Ω_{\rm m},w_0,w_a) = (0.305\pm0.004,-0.861^{+0.044}_{-0.042},-0.60^{+0.17}_{-0.19})$ with a dark energy Figure of Merit of 315. This corresponds to a $\sim30\%$ reduction in the area of the $w_0-w_a$ confidence region relative to previous constraints from the combination of DES Y6, DESI-DR2, and CMB data (arXiv:2605.27221). The Bayesian evidence indicates only weak preference for time evolving dark energy, whereas frequentist analyses yield a preference over Flat-$Λ$CDM at a significance of $2.5σ$ when using the maximum $\mathit{a\ posteriori}$ probability, or $3.1σ$ when using the maximum likelihood.

AI.tldr: This paper presents Unite, the combination of the Pantheon+ and DES-SN5YR supernova samples, creating the most comprehensive internally consistent dataset of 2884 type Ia supernovae. Using Unite alone, they find Ωm = 0.310 for flat ΛCDM. When combined with CMB and BAO data, they find tension between CMB and combined BAO+SN data under constant dark energy equation of state, which is alleviated when allowing w to vary with time, yielding (Ωm, w0, wa) = (0.305, -0.861, -0.60) with a 30% reduction in the w0-wa confidence region area.
AI.motivation: To provide the most comprehensive and internally consistent type Ia supernova dataset by combining the Pantheon+ and DES-SN5YR samples with uniform methodology, sample selection, bias corrections, and host-galaxy stellar mass determinations, in order to derive improved cosmological constraints on dark energy.
AI.method: Combines the Pantheon+ and DES-SN5YR supernova samples into a unified dataset called Unite, incorporating methodology improvements enabled by the DES sample. Applies consistent SN Ia modelling, sample selection, and bias corrections, and redetermines host-galaxy stellar masses for over 98% of the sample using a consistent framework. Analyzes the sample alone for flat ΛCDM, and in combination with CMB and DES/DESI BAO data under constant and time-evolving dark energy equation of state models, using both Bayesian and frequentist statistical approaches.
AI.result: From Unite alone (flat ΛCDM): Ωm = 0.310^{+0.012}_{-0.011}. Combined with CMB and BAO data under evolving w0-wa model: (Ωm, w0, wa) = (0.305±0.004, -0.861^{+0.044}_{-0.042}, -0.60^{+0.17}_{-0.19}) with dark energy Figure of Merit of 315, a ~30% reduction in w0-wa confidence region area versus prior constraints. Tension between CMB and combined BAO+SN data is found under constant w, alleviated when allowing w to vary with time. Dark energy figure of merit is 315. Bayesian evidence shows only weak preference for evolving dark energy, while frequentist analyses show preference over flat ΛCDM at 2.5σ (MAP) or 3.1σ (maximum likelihood).
AI.conclusion: The Unite dataset provides the most comprehensive and internally consistent SN Ia sample to date. The combined cosmological constraints suggest a mild preference for time-evolving dark energy at 2.5-3.1σ by frequentist measures (though only weak by Bayesian evidence), and demonstrate improved constraining power with a 30% reduction in the w0-wa parameter space compared to previous combined results.

title: H I Absorbers as Beacons of Hidden Structure at $z \sim 3$: Multi-Component, Metal-Rich Absorption System near a Protocluster
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 17 pages, 19 figures
summary: H I gas traces the large-scale structure and provides the primary fuel for star formation. High-$z$ protoclusters are ideal laboratories to study how H I gas is accreted and consumed during the formation of the most massive structures in the Universe. However, much remains unknown about the distribution and physical state of their H I gas. We examine a rare configuration in which a protocluster candidate is located in front of a quasar at $z=3.09$. Our spectroscopic campaign confirms a protocluster at $z=3.079$: however, no corresponding strong H I absorption is found in the background quasar spectrum. Instead, we serendipitously discover a prominent H I absorption feature at $z\sim 3.01$, offset by $\sim 60$ cMpc from the centre of the protocluster. Spanning an exceptionally broad velocity range of $\sim 2000$ km s$^{-1}$ ($\sim 40$ cMpc), this absorption is decoupled from the confirmed member galaxies. Detailed kinematic modelling reveals this absorption comprises five distinct components rather than a single cloud. Moreover, one of these components exhibits a super-solar metallicity ($[\mathrm{O/H}] = +1.19^{+0.91}_{-0.78}$). We propose two physical scenarios for this unique system: (1) an additional, hidden massive protocluster along the line of sight, and/or (2) metal-rich outflows and metal-poor inflows driven by a single massive galaxy. The discovery highlights that while protoclusters are not universally associated with strong H I absorption, targeting the strong H I absorbers may serve as a beacon for uncovering massive, metal-rich protoclusters or complex gas kinematics in the early Universe.

AI.tldr: A protocluster candidate at z=3.079 shows no strong H I absorption in a background quasar spectrum, but reveals a serendipitous broad (~2000 km/s) H I absorption feature ~60 cMpc away at z~3.01, comprising five kinematic components including one super-solar metallicity component. This suggests either a hidden massive protocluster along the line of sight or interactions between metal-rich outflows and metal-poor inflows from a single massive galaxy.
AI.motivation: To understand how H I gas is distributed and accreted during the formation of massive structures (protoclusters) at high redshift, using the rare alignment of a protocluster candidate in front of a background quasar to probe H I absorption.
AI.method: Spectroscopic campaign to confirm a protocluster at z=3.079; examination of background quasar spectrum for H I absorption; detailed kinematic modelling of a discovered H I absorption feature at z~3.01 including component analysis and metallicity estimation.
AI.result: No strong H I absorption associated with the confirmed protocluster. Instead, a broad H I absorption spanning ~2000 km/s (~40 cMpc) was found offset ~60 cMpc from the protocluster center, resolved into five distinct kinematic components, one with super-solar metallicity ([O/H]=+1.19).
AI.conclusion: Protoclusters are not universally associated with strong H I absorption. The discovery suggests strong H I absorbers could serve as tracers for uncovering massive, metal-rich protoclusters or complex gas kinematics in the early Universe. Two scenarios are proposed: a hidden massive protocluster along the line of sight, or metal-rich outflows and metal-poor inflows from a massive galaxy.

title: Euclid. A two-point correlation approach to diagnosing star-related systematics in the Euclid spectroscopic survey
summary: The Euclid spectroscopic survey will measure galaxy clustering with unprecedented precision, requiring stringent control of observational and instrumental systematics. Star-related effects may contaminate spectroscopic images through photometric persistence and imperfect masking of stars. We characterized their impact on galaxy clustering analyses, focusing on angular features identifiable in the data. We used angular and spatial auto- and cross-correlation statistics. For galaxies, we used mock spectroscopic catalogues from the EuclidLargeMocks in a 330 deg2 region of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS). For stars, we used Gaia and 2MASS catalogues in the same area. To simulate photometric persistence, we implemented a simplified detector-level model calibrated on spectroscopic measurements and varied its strength to introduce different interloper fractions. For stellar masking, we modelled inconsistencies between the mask applied to the data and to the random catalogue. We measured star-star, galaxy-galaxy, and star-galaxy angular correlation functions using the Landy--Szalay estimator, and quantified deviations from the expected null star-galaxy correlation. We also evaluated the large-scale impact of such systematics through the three-dimensional two-point correlation function (2PCF). Photometric persistence produces a characteristic feature in the star-galaxy angular cross-correlation at scales of order 100", corresponding to the Euclid dithering pattern and grism dispersion geometry, and a spurious positive signal approximately constant up to 1°. Star-galaxy cross-correlation can detect residual persistence at contamination levels as low as 10% in a Data Release 1 spectroscopic catalogue. In contrast, stellar-mask mismatches produce strong small-scale angular signatures but have negligible impact on the large-scale 2PCF under realistic EWS conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes how star-related systematics (photometric persistence and imperfect stellar masking) contaminate Euclid spectroscopic galaxy clustering measurements. Using mock galaxy catalogues and real star catalogues, the authors show photometric persistence produces a characteristic angular cross-correlation feature at ~100" scales (detectable down to 10% contamination), while stellar-mask mismatches cause strong small-scale angular signatures but negligible impact on large-scale clustering.
AI.motivation: The Euclid spectroscopic survey demands unprecedented precision in galaxy clustering measurements, which requires tight control of observational and instrumental systematics. Star-related effects such as photometric persistence and imperfect stellar masking can contaminate spectroscopic data and bias clustering analyses if not properly characterized and mitigated.
AI.method: The authors use angular and spatial auto-/cross-correlation statistics on mock Euclid spectroscopic catalogues (EuclidLargeMocks) in a 330 deg² EWS region combined with Gaia and 2MASS star catalogues. They simulate photometric persistence via a simplified detector-level model with variable strength to introduce different interloper fractions, and model stellar-mask inconsistencies between data and random catalogues. They employ the Landy–Szalay estimator for angular correlations and the 3D two-point correlation function for large-scale impact.
AI.result: Photometric persistence creates a distinctive star-galaxy angular cross-correlation signature at ~100" scales, matching Euclid's dithering pattern and grism dispersion geometry, plus a spurious positive signal constant out to ~1°. The star-galaxy cross-correlation can detect persistence down to 10% contamination levels in a Data Release 1 catalog. Stellar-mask mismatches produce strong small-scale angular signatures but negligible effects on the large-scale 2PCF under realistic EWS conditions.
AI.conclusion: Star-galaxy angular cross-correlations provide an effective diagnostic for detecting photometric persistence contamination in Euclid spectroscopic data, while stellar-mask mismatches are less concerning for large-scale clustering analyses. The characteristic angular signatures identified can serve as practical validation tools for systematics control in the Euclid survey.

title: Extending the Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relation to Dwarf Galaxies with DESI DR1
comment: 23 pages (+4 pages of appendices), 11 figures. Comments are welcome!
summary: Constraining the dark matter halos of the smallest galaxies offers fundamental insights into the nature of dark matter and stellar feedback. Using the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 1, we infer the stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR) down to the dwarf scale ($M_\star < 10^9\,M_\odot$), without extrapolation from the higher mass range. Leveraging the unprecedented depth of the DESI Bright Galaxy Survey at $0.01 < z < 0.2$, we construct 12 samples spanning nearly four orders of magnitude in stellar mass, and measure their projected clustering $w_p$, galaxy-galaxy lensing $ΔΣ$, as well as a novel observable: satellite occupation number $N_{\rm sat}$. The addition of $N_{\rm sat}$ enables robust subtraction of satellite contributions to both $w_p$ and $ΔΣ$ across the 12 individual halo occupation distribution analyses, yielding an average halo-to-stellar mass relation (HSMR) of $\log \langle M_h(M_\star) \rangle = 12.06 + 0.58\log(M_\star/10^{11}) + (M_\star/10^{11})^{0.73}$. Combining this HSMR with an observed stellar mass function, we constrain the SHMR across five orders of magnitude in halo mass, with the power-law slope steepening from $0.32 \pm 0.06$ above the Milky Way mass to $2.08 \pm 0.21$ in the dwarf regime. Interestingly, the scatter about the SHMR grows from $0.17 \pm 0.02$ dex at Milky Way-like scales to $0.68_{-0.33}^{+0.21}$ dex for systems comparable to the Large Magellanic Cloud, suggesting that smaller galaxies follow increasingly diverse evolutionary paths. Our work highlights the power of DESI in probing the galaxy-halo connection within the dwarf regime, offering an exciting avenue to bridge the gap between large-scale and near-field cosmologies in the future.

AI.tldr: Using DESI Data Release 1, the authors constrain the stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR) down to dwarf-galaxy scales (M_star < 10^9 M_sun) by combining projected clustering, galaxy-galaxy lensing, and a novel satellite occupation number observable across 12 samples. Each sample is analyzed with an individual halo occupation distribution (HOD) model, where N_sat enables robust subtraction of satellite contributions to both w_p and ΔΣ.

Combined with the observed stellar mass function, this constrains the SHMR across five orders of magnitude in halo mass. AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates DESI's power in probing the galaxy-halo connection in the dwarf regime without extrapolation, revealing steepening SHMR slopes and increasing scatter toward small masses. title: Supernovae Unite: Host-Galaxy Mass Measurements of Type Ia Supernovae and Their Impact on Cosmology
comment: 26 pages, 9 figures. Companion paper to Supernovae Unite: Combining Pantheon+ and DES-SN5YR
summary: Current consensus suggests that Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) brightnesses post light-curve standardization correlate with their host-galaxy stellar masses, which must be accounted for to obtain accurate cosmological constraints. Vincenzi et al. (2025) showed that different host-galaxy stellar mass measurements for the same dataset can produce redshift-dependent differences of order $\sim 0.01$ mag. We quantify the impact of photometry and SED fitting choices on SN-Unite cosmological parameters in Flat$w$CDM and find shifts well below statistical uncertainties. Our stellar masses differ from the Pantheon+ data release partly due to a redshift-dependent internal inconsistency within Pantheon+, while remaining largely consistent with DES-SN5YR (DES-Dovekie). When the Pantheon+ subsample of SN-Unite is combined with Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) and Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) measurements, the significance for time-evolving dark energy increases from 2.6$σ$ to 3.4$σ$ based on the maximum \textit{a posteriori} when our newly derived host-galaxy stellar masses replace the Pantheon+ data-release host-galaxy stellar masses, while DES-Dovekie remains virtually unchanged, consistent with the findings of Hoyt et al. (2026). By remeasuring the host-galaxy stellar masses using a consistent framework throughout the whole sample, we improve the robustness of the SN-Unite cosmological constraints against systematic differences in host-galaxy stellar mass measurements.

They find photometry/SED choice shifts are negligible for cosmology, uncover a redshift-dependent inconsistency in Pantheon+ masses, and show that their corrected masses increase the significance for time-evolving dark energy from 2.6σ to 3.4σ when combined with BAO and CMB.
AI.motivation: SN Ia brightness after light-curve standardization correlates with host-galaxy stellar mass, and different host mass measurements can introduce redshift-dependent systematics (~0.01 mag) affecting cosmological constraints. The authors aim to provide internally consistent host masses across the largest SN Ia sample to improve robustness of cosmological parameter estimation.
AI.method: The authors performed aperture photometry and spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting to remeasure host-galaxy stellar masses for all SN-Unite host galaxies (2884 likely SNe Ia from Pantheon+ and DES-SN5YR). They quantified the impact of photometric and SED-fitting choice variations on FlatwCDM parameters and compared their masses against the Pantheon+ and DES-SN5YR (DES-Dovekie) data releases, then re-analyzed cosmological constraints (including DES+Delve, BAO, and CMB) with the new masses.
AI.result: Stellar-mass choice shifts on cosmological parameters were well below statistical uncertainties. title: Hint of bimodal Mg-Al anticorrelation in the metal-poor Globular Cluster NGC 4372
comment: 11 pages, 12 figures
summary: We present a detailed chemical abundance analysis of seven red giant branch stars in the very metal-poor globular cluster NGC~4372, based on high-resolution UVES spectra. We derived abundances for 17 elements, including light, iron-peak, $α$, and heavy elements, using both equivalent width and spectral synthesis methods. We find a mean cluster metallicity of [Fe/H]=$-$2.36 $\pm$ 0.03 dex, with no evidence of an intrinsic iron spread. The cluster exhibits a typical $α$-enhancement of [$α$/Fe]= 0.33 $\pm$ 0.05 dex and a well defined Na-O anticorrelation, confirming that NGC 4372 hosts at least two distinct stellar populations. Furthermore, the measured ratio of [Ba/Eu] =$-0.47 \pm 0.04$ indicates that the synthesis of heavy elements was dominated by $r$-process, consistent with other very metal-poor environments. We also identify a potential bimodal Mg-Al anticorrelation, which aligns with the patterns observed in GCs of similar mass and metallicity. These results reinforce the status of NGC 4372 as a cornerstone for understanding the early chemical enrichment of the Galactic Halo.

AI.method: High-resolution UVES spectroscopy of seven red giant branch stars; abundances for 17 elements (light, iron-peak, alpha, and heavy elements) derived using both equivalent width and spectral synthesis methods.
